data.title: Recurrent PIK3CA-E545K mutation promotes cervical cancer growth and invasion via AKT/mTOR signaling.
data.authors: Huang C; Zhang W; Ma X; Li X; Sun X

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: PIK3CA-E545K hotspot mutation enhances cervical cancer cell proliferation and invasion by activating AKT/mTOR signaling, validated in xenograft models.
data.abstract_excerpt: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality among women worldwide. Although genomic alterations in oncogenic signaling pathways have been implicated in cervical carcinogenesis, the functional impact of recurrent driver mutations remains incompletely understood. Whole-exome sequencing was performed on paired tumor and matched non-tumor tissues from 61 patients to identify recurrent somatic alterations.

extracted_findings.effect: Promotes tumor cell proliferation and invasion
